rejectedSkills.reason: Every actionable step in the workflow (Determine the Mode / Generate from Text / Generate from Image / Edit / Generate Variants) is a direct call to a Stitch MCP tool (list_projects, generate_screen_from_text, edit_screens, generate_variants, apply_design_system) reachable only with the Stitch MCP server and an authenticated Google account -- both undeclared external services this registry cannot assume. Without that MCP connection an agent literally cannot execute any of the six numbered flows; the only content that survives without Stitch is the prompt-enhancement vocabulary in references/design-mappings.md and references/prompt-keywords.md, which is thin generic advice on its own and does not clear the quality bar by itself. Per the brief's instruction to weigh relevance/uniqueness honestly for Stitch-gated skills, scored below the vendor threshold.

Pure orchestrator with no independent instructional content of its own -- every step is 'delegate to the X skill, read skills/X/SKILL.md'. Its SKILL.md relative links (../extract-static-html/SKILL.md, ../extract-design-md/SKILL.md, ../manage-design-system/SKILL.md, ../upload-to-stitch/SKILL.md) point at sibling skill directories outside its own; two of those siblings (manage-design-system, upload-to-stitch) are separately rejected here as Stitch-only with no standalone value, so vendoring code-to-design alone leaves broken links, and bundling all four just to satisfy the self-containment rule would duplicate independently-rejected skills inside it. Its entire purpose -- turning existing frontend code into a Stitch project screen -- has no meaning without the Stitch MCP server and API key it hands off to at steps 4-5.

Entirely a sequence of Stitch MCP API calls (get_screen, create_design_system_from_design_md, apply_design_system, list_design_systems) with no design judgment content of its own -- it is CRUD-over-MCP instructions, not design guidance. It also repeatedly defers structure and best-practice content to 'the design-md skill (in the stitch-utilities plugin)', a different plugin outside the assigned plugins/stitch-design/skills/ scope and not fetched -- an external dependency the self-containment rule cannot resolve. No standalone value without a Stitch MCP connection and a project already holding screens to manage.

A generic base64/multipart file-upload script and its CLI instructions, whose sole purpose is POSTing a file to the Stitch v1 REST API (stitch.googleapis.com) with a Stitch API key. Self-contained and conformant (its only reference is to its own bundled scripts/upload_to_stitch.py), but there is no design judgment or transferable technique here -- it has zero standalone value outside a Stitch project and account, and is closer to generic infrastructure tooling than design work.

securityNotes: Read every SKILL.md in full; skimmed scripts/upload_to_stitch.py (268 lines, python3, urllib.request POST to a caller-supplied --api-url defaulting to https://stitch.googleapis.com, api key passed explicitly by the user via --api-key CLI arg, no hidden endpoints, no credential harvesting beyond what the user supplies on the command line). No hidden instructions, prompt injection, or exfiltration found in any of the four rejected skills.
logMd:
#### google-labs-code/stitch-skills -- rejections (inspected 2026-08-26)

See stitch-extract-design-md.json for shared repo evidence (HEAD 0337446dadde6f8c94210444e2aa9d546126480f, 8213 stars, Apache-2.0 confirmed at repo-root LICENSE). Of the six skills under plugins/stitch-design/skills/ at this pinned commit, four are rejected here: generate-design, code-to-design, manage-design-system, upload-to-stitch. All four are entirely wrappers around the Stitch MCP server and/or the Stitch HTTP API and a Google-authenticated Stitch account -- none has a working path without that private service, so per the task brief's instruction to weigh relevance/uniqueness honestly rather than reflexively vendor with a stitch-mcp dependency tag, each scored below the vendor threshold (total 4-5, all under the required 6). manage-design-system and code-to-design additionally fail conformance outright: both link to skill directories outside plugins/stitch-design/skills/ (manage-design-system references the 'design-md' skill in the separate stitch-utilities plugin, never fetched; code-to-design references upload-to-stitch and manage-design-system, two skills rejected here) that the self-containment rule cannot resolve without bundling independently-rejected content. The two skills from this plugin judged to have real standalone value -- extract-design-md (reads source code, writes a DESIGN.md design-system document, no MCP calls in its core path) and extract-static-html (Puppeteer/browser-based static HTML snapshot capture, no MCP calls) -- are vendored separately in stitch-extract-design-md.json and stitch-extract-static-html.json.
